source: make the backrooms horror movie map. add elements using procedural models

image_prompt.text: Alcoves and recesses cut into the wallpapered walls where a player can break line of sight and hide
Enterable back rooms and side offices opening off the main corridors
A structural door set into the outer wall of the warren, the one way out of the level
An interconnected maze of dim, repetitive rooms and corridors in the style of the Backrooms from horror media

layout_placement.text: The exit door acts as the round-win trigger

notes: Classified Survival over a Puzzle maze because the prompt frames it as horror rather than as a solvable route; it was a close call and Entertainment Showcase was a third reading, since the prompt asks for a map rather than a game.
Looping Warren routes P6, which happens to align with the user asking for procedural models; the zero-dead-ends property cannot be guaranteed by a free image.
Escape preset carries building-interior, which is why P3 is present even though the whole map reads as one continuous interior.
The prompt names a known reference (the Backrooms) and expects it to carry the art direction; nothing in the handoff records that dependency.

open_questions.ask: Is there a threat chasing the player and an exit to reach, or is this purely a space to wander?
How large should the maze be before it starts repeating?

coverage_missing.ask: Is something hunting the player in here, and is there a way out, or is the point to be lost?
Roughly how big should the maze be?
Does procedural models mean generated geometry at runtime, or just modular repeated pieces?

answers.ask: Is there a threat chasing the player and an exit to reach, or is this purely a space to wander?
answers.answer: Make it a purely atmospheric space to wander; the prompt does not call for a chasing threat or an exit objective.

answers.ask: How large should the maze be before it starts repeating?
answers.answer: Keep it small: build a compact maze of roughly 12–16 rooms and corridors before repeating procedural sections.
